q: Which country has the longest coastline in the world?
x: Canada's coastline is about 202,000 km, thanks to its thousands of Arctic islands. That's more than five times around the Equator.

q: Which planet rotates on its side?
x: Uranus is tilted about 98°, probably from a huge collision long ago, so each pole gets about 42 years of daylight.

q: What is the national animal of Scotland?
x: It's been a Scottish royal symbol since the 1300s and still appears on the UK coat of arms.

q: In which country is Timbuktu?
x: It was a major center of trade and Islamic scholarship in the 1400s and 1500s, on the edge of the Sahara.

q: How many time zones does China officially use?
x: China spans about five time zones' width but runs on Beijing time, so the sun can rise around 10 a.m. in the far west.

q: Measured from base to peak, which is the tallest mountain on Earth?
x: Mauna Kea rises about 10,200 m from the Pacific floor. Everest is the highest above sea level, at 8,849 m.

q: Who painted The Persistence of Memory, the one with the melting clocks?
x: Dalí painted it in 1931. It hangs in the Museum of Modern Art in New York.

q: The shortest war in recorded history lasted under an hour. Who fought it?
x: In 1896 the Anglo-Zanzibar War lasted between 38 and 45 minutes.

q: Which country has the most pyramids?
x: Sudan's ancient Nubian kingdoms built more than 200 pyramids, almost twice as many as Egypt.

q: Who was the first woman to fly solo across the Atlantic?
x: She did it in 1932, five years after Lindbergh. Harriet Quimby was the first woman to fly across the English Channel.

q: Which of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World is still standing?
x: It's also the oldest of the seven, by about 2,000 years.

q: What is the capital of Turkey?
x: Atatürk made Ankara the capital in 1923. Istanbul is the largest city.

q: Who was the second person to walk on the Moon?
x: Aldrin followed Neil Armstrong out about 19 minutes later. Michael Collins stayed in orbit.

q: What is the largest moon in the solar system?
x: Jupiter's Ganymede is bigger than the planet Mercury. Saturn's Titan is a close second.

q: Who is the longest-reigning British monarch?
x: She reigned for 70 years, from 1952 to 2022. Victoria is second, at 63 years.

q: Which composer wrote his Ninth Symphony while almost completely deaf?
x: At the 1824 premiere, he had to be turned around to see the audience applauding.

q: Which city was once called New Amsterdam?
x: The English took it from the Dutch in 1664 and renamed it after the Duke of York.

q: During protein synthesis, which molecule carries amino acids to the ribosome?
x: Each tRNA has an anticodon that pairs with a codon on the mRNA, so the right amino acid gets added.

q: Two 10-ohm resistors connected in parallel have a combined resistance of…
x: In parallel, the current has two paths, so the resistance drops. Equal resistors in parallel give half the value. In series, it would be 20.

q: Which country gets the most international tourists?
x: France gets about 100 million foreign visitors a year. Spain is usually second.
